items.content_text:
What stories change the dominant narrative?
 We invite local artists and creatives to participate in The People’s Gallery, a month-long exhibition exploring Chattanooga’s grassroots histories of labor, civil rights, racial justice, white supremacy, resistance, and community power.
 The exhibition builds on The People’s History Tour. A foundation for understanding the people who organized, resisted, cared for one another and changed the course of our city. But history is never finished, and no single tour or exhibition can tell the whole story.
 That is where artists come in.
 We’re inviting artists to help us uncover, question and carry forward the stories that have been overlooked, erased, misunderstood or left unfinished.
 There are two ways to participate:
 1️⃣ THE PEOPLE’S HISTORY POSTER COMPETITION
 Submit a portfolio by September 4 for the chance to be selected as one of three artists creating an original 12 × 18" poster responding to the question: What stories change the dominant narrative? Three artists will compete for $2,000 in prizes, with the winning designs unveiled at The People’s Gallery event on October 24.
 2️⃣ THE PEOPLE’S GALLERY EXHIBITION
 Submit existing or original work exploring the themes of The People’s Gallery for inclusion in our month-long exhibition at Stove Works this October. Submissions are due September 18.
 Learn more and apply: calebcha.org/peoples-gallery
 Artists are encouraged to honor what is theirs to tell and the boundaries of others.
 We want to see the stories that deserve to be seen, heard, remembered, questioned and carried forward.

Traffic Fatality - 7100 Shallowford Rd.
 CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. -- The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) Traffic/DUI Unit was informed by the Hamilton County Medical Examiner's Office that a driver from an August 17, 2026 crash died from the injuries she sustained. The two-vehicle crash occurred near 7100 Shallowford Road within the intersection of the Interstate 75 exit ramp. 
 Through investigation, interview, and observation CPD's Traffic/DUI investigators determined Vehicle 1 (Ford Edge) was exiting I-75 Northbound when, for unknown reasons, it drove through a red light and collided with Vehicle 2 (Toyota Avalon). 
 Hamilton County EMS transported the driver of Vehicle 1 to a local hospital. The driver of Vehicle 2 sustained minor injuries and was not taken to a hospital. CPD was notified that the driver of Vehicle 1, a 73-year-old woman, succumbed to her injuries on August 22, 2026. 
 #CPDNews

COLLEGEDALE COMMISSION INVESTS IN POLICE STAFFING
 COLLEGEDALE, TN (08/24/2026) - The Collegedale Police Department has hired four additional police officers, increasing the department’s full-time sworn strength from 29 to 33 officers.
 The new positions were made possible through the continued support of the Collegedale City Commission and its commitment to investing in public safety, officer safety, and the level of service provided to the community.
 “We are grateful to the members of the Collegedale City Commission for recognizing the importance of maintaining appropriate staffing as our community continues to grow and change,” Police Chief Jack Sapp said. “Their support allows us to strengthen our department, provide our officers with additional resources and backup, and continue delivering the level of service Collegedale residents expect.”
 All four new officers will be assigned to the Patrol Division, increasing patrol staffing from 19 to 23 officers. Patrol officers provide the department’s around-the-clock response to calls for service, traffic safety, neighborhood and business patrols, crash investigations, and other public safety needs throughout the city.
 The additional officers will improve the department’s ability to maintain consistent patrol coverage when personnel are unavailable because of training, vacation, illness, court appearances, or other obligations. The increased staffing will also provide greater flexibility for officer backup, proactive policing, traffic safety, and community engagement.
 The department’s responsibilities extend beyond Collegedale’s residential population. Each day, thousands of additional people enter the city to work, attend school, shop, visit businesses, and travel through the community. The additional officers will help the department meet those demands while maintaining a strong public safety presence throughout Collegedale.
 “The City Commission’s decision is an investment not only in the people who live, work, attend school, and travel through Collegedale, but also in the men and women who serve this community around the clock,” Sapp said. “These additional officers will strengthen officer safety and help us continue providing professional, responsive service to our community.”
 The Collegedale Police Department extends its sincere appreciation to the Collegedale City Commission for recognizing the department’s staffing needs and taking meaningful action to support the officers who serve the community.

HCSO Recovers Gun from Ooltewah High School, Juvenile Charged
 Hamilton County, TN – On the morning of August 24, 2026, HCSO K-9 Unit deputies responded to Ooltewah High School to assist the assigned school resource deputy (SRD) and the school’s administration with a report of a potential firearm on campus.
 An HCSO K-9 alerted to a vehicle in the school’s parking lot, initiating a search that recovered a loaded firearm, magazine, and multiple additional rounds of ammunition.
 A juvenile suspect was taken into custody and charged with the following: 
 • Possession of a Firearm on School Property
 This is an example of the important partnership that the HCSO and Hamilton County Department of Education have in ensuring the safety of our students.
 This information is preliminary and subject to change. No further details are available.

Connecting people with opportunity is at the heart of workforce development.

Recently, members of our workforce development team, Lauri Wilson and Gloria Freeman, attended the Athens Job Fair, connecting with job seekers and 20 other employers from across the region.

For someone looking for their next opportunity, knowing where to start can make all the difference. Our team shared resources available through the local workforce system, including job search assistance through JOBS4TN, resume development, career counseling, job readiness support, and information about WIOA Title I education and training opportunities for eligible participants.

This is an important part of the work happening through SETD that we look forward to sharing more about: connecting people to careers, helping employers find talent, and strengthening Southeast Tennessee’s workforce one connection at a time.

We’re proud of our workforce team for continuing to meet people where they are and connect them with the tools and opportunities to move forward!

items.content_text:
🚧📹 New Technology Alert! Better Stormwater Protection for Red Bank! 🌧️
 The City of Red Bank's Public Works Stormwater Division is excited to put their new pipe inspection camera into service, giving our team a safer and more efficient way to inspect underground stormwater infrastructure!
 This past Friday, the stormwater team met with City Manager Martin Granum, Mayor Stephanie Dalton, and Public Works Director Greg Tate to demonstrate the new capabilities that this device offers. With this new camera, the team will be able to inspect underground stormwater assets quickly and safely, helping to ensure that the stormwater system is ready to weather future storms.
 By allowing crews to identify blockages, structural concerns, and other issues without extensive excavation, this technology will help improve maintenance efforts and protect critical infrastructure throughout our community.
 If you see the stormwater division team members on the side of the road using this camera, please give them space to work safely and proceed with caution around their work zone.
 Investing in modern equipment helps our team work smarter, safer, and more effectively as we continue to serve the citizens of Red Bank. 💙
 #RedBankTN #PublicWorks #StormwaterManagement

 How is RBC being taken up in company practices and government policies?
 The #OECD Responsible Business Outlook shows that less than 2 in 10 companies have formal processes in place to assess human rights complaints and less than 1 in 10 companies engage with stakeholders on human rights issues.

The word "transformed" is powerful and yet, in this instance, it feels inadequate.  Yesterday, East Ridge residents and friends joined Mayor Brian Williams, City Council and staff in re-opening the East Ridge Community Center.  It was a great day in East Ridge !
 After years of planning and work and more than $2.3M in improvements, the Community Center now stands ready to serve the next generation at the center of our city.  
 ✅ Expanded gym with full size basketball court
 ✅ Three indoor pickleball courts
 ✅ Refreshed bathrooms and public spaces
 ✅ Upgraded kitchen and community rooms
 ✅ The coolest mural in town
 Thanks for your patience as we've made these investments in our park system.  We can't wait to welcome you home to the Community Center in the weeks ahead !

items.content_text:
Financial scams and frauds are a serious risk for consumers around the world, threatening both their financial well-being and trust in the financial system.
 #OECD analysis covering 69 jurisdictions shows that in 2024, 70% of them experienced an increase in scams and frauds.
 Scams and frauds also resulted in a total of USD 10 billion in reported losses to public authorities in 36 jurisdictions.
 As digital finance expands, fraudsters are increasingly using AI, deepfakes and sophisticated online techniques to target consumers, many of whom are not well equipped to spot the risks.
 To address this issue, the OECD categorises financial scams and frauds to help public authorities better classify and use reported data.
 Read about key OECD policy recommendations on the issue ➡️ https://brnw.ch/21x58Kh

Giving a voice to multilingual exchange.
 Multilingual communication is at the heart of successful, effective and inclusive international co-operation, and the #OECD’s teams of interpreters work tirelessly from the sidelines to ensure that delegations’ messages are conveyed accurately and faithfully in several languages simultaneously.
 This year, interpretation in French, English and Spanish was provided for all the #OECDministerial sessions, with Japanese and Italian also being added on several occasions. Every word spoken in one language is instantly conveyed in all the other languages by our teams of professional interpreters, meaning that delegations can think, react, speak and listen in the language of their choice.
 In this way, the interpreters open gateways between different cultures during high-level discussions on international issues.

Tennessee American Water Completes Tank Hoist
 New 750,000-Gallon Tank Doubles Water Storage Capacity
 [Chattanooga, TN] – August 21, 2026 – Tennessee American Water, in coordination with its contractor Landmark Structures, has completed the tank hoist of its new Lookout Valley water storage tank. Once in service, the tank will hold 750,000 gallons of treated water, doubling water storage capacity for the Lookout Valley area.
 The new tank is one of several infrastructure improvements included in Tennessee American Water's capital investment program, which is expected to total more than $45 million in 2026.
 "This project represents an important investment in the reliability and resilience of our water system," said Grant Evitts, President of Tennessee American Water. "The additional storage will strengthen our ability to meet customer demand, respond to emergencies, and provide reliable service for years to come."
 The welded steel tank bowl was constructed on the ground, centered around a concrete pedestal measuring approximately 95 feet tall. After construction and coating work were completed, a crane lifted the tank bowl into place atop the pedestal. When placed into service, the tank will provide additional operational flexibility and redundancy for customers served in the Lookout Valley area of the Citico distribution system.
 Tanks are an important part of the distribution system, located in elevated areas where gravity can assist with the delivery of treated water through pipes to homes and businesses. Tennessee American Water has 20 tanks located in its Citico service area, which serves Chattanooga, East Ridge, Lookout Mountain and Red Bank in Tennessee as well as communities in northwest Georgia. The new tank is located adjacent to an existing elevated water storage tank of the same capacity.
 Landmark Structures is a leading provider of engineering, construction, and asset management services for storage solutions in the water, wastewater, power, and industrial markets in North America.
 ABOUT AMERICAN WATER
 American Water (NYSE: AWK) is the largest regulated water and wastewater utility company in the United States. With a history dating back to 1886 and celebrating 140 years in 2026, We Keep Life Flowing® by providing safe, clean, reliable and affordable drinking water and wastewater services to approximately 14 million people with regulated operations in 14 states and on 19 military installations. American Water’s approximately 7,000 talented professionals leverage their significant expertise and the company’s national size and scale to achieve excellent outcomes for the benefit of customers, employees, investors and other stakeholders. 
 ABOUT TENNESSEE AMERICAN WATER
 Tennessee American Water, a subsidiary of American Water, is the largest regulated water utility in the state with approximately 100 dedicated employees working to provide safe, clean, reliable and affordable water services to approximately 425,000 people in Tennessee and north Georgia.
  
 For more information, visit www.tennesseeamwater.com and connect with us on Facebook, X, Instagram, LinkedIn and YouTube.

 Real GDP per capita in the United Kingdom increased by 0.6% after two quarters with no growth. 
 Among other #OECD countries, the largest increases in real household income per capita were recorded in Hungary and Chile. 
 GDP growth focuses on the change in aggregate economic activity, while household income growth reflects the change in income earned by households such as the income available for spending or saving.

Chattanooga Police and Fire responded to the 400 block of Northmont Road Friday (8/21/26) morning at 11:24 AM after a homeowner discovered an old bottle in their garage containing a hazardous substance- Diethyl Ether Anhydrous. A small evacuation of four homes was initiated as a safety measure, including the home involved. Other neighbors have been asked to shelter in place. Chattanooga Police Department EOD will be assisting CFD Special Operations in the removal of the substance. Part of Northmont Road is closed to traffic for the time being. No airborne hazards or other safety threats are involved in this incident.

The Urban League of Greater Chattanooga hosted its 11th annual Entrepreneur Power Luncheon this week.
 We were honored to have Chef Jason Gardner as our keynote speaker. Jason Darnell Gardner, known as Chef JGardner, is a Memphis native and founder of TrapFusion901, a restaurant celebrated for its creative and healthy soul food. His culinary journey began at age seven with his grandmother’s influence, leading to the opening of Trap Fusion in Whitehaven in 2019. After studying Biology at The University of Tennessee at Chattanooga, he explored various entrepreneurial ventures, including event planning and the launch of BeLeaf Cigars. In 2018, he returned to cooking with a food truck, quickly gaining a loyal following. Today, Chef JGardner caters to celebrities and remains dedicated to investing in his community.
 We also honored two local entrepreneurs!
 ULGC’s New Business of the Year: Darryl Eubanks II, the founder and owner of Still Life Athletics 
 ULGC’s Business of the Year: Cheryl Key, John P. Franklin Funeral Home 
 We would also like to thank our presenting sponsor, EPB; Capital Access Sponsors, Pinnacle Financial Partners, Tennessee Valley Federal Credit Union, and Hamilton County Mayor’s Office!
 Images:  Final Flash Productions

Meet Ms. Wanda. 💙💛
 For more than 36 years, Wanda Goins has been a familiar face at UTC. From ushering at McKenzie Arena to working security in the James R. Mapp Building, she has spent decades welcoming, helping and connecting with students, faculty, staff and visitors across campus.
 You may also know her as “Wanda the Program Lady” at Chattanooga Lookouts games, where she has been a familiar face since 1990.
 This week, Wanda was inducted into the Bessie Smith Cultural Center Hall of Fame in recognition of her contributions to the Chattanooga community.
 Her secret to staying positive? “I don’t meet no strangers. I just enjoy people.”
 We’re proud to call Ms. Wanda a Moc and grateful for all the ways she has helped make UTC and Chattanooga feel like home. 💙💛
 🔗  Read more here: https://blog.utc.edu/…/the-people-of-utc-get-to-know-miss-…/

Imagine a space where you can live, work, dine, and play — that’s what’s coming soon to Broad Street as we celebrate the groundbreaking of Station 33. When complete, this development will feature 91 mixed residential units, a 25,000-sqft commercial space, a dining hall, and a European-style plaza in the center where all residents can gather for events and family-friendly fun.  
 We have been working very hard behind the scenes on reforming our Land Development Office to make it easier for Chattanooga to do business with the kind of visionaries behind this project. There are opportunities to create great urban environments where we have brownfields, as we’ve seen developed in other cities around the country. Station 33 will be a monumental addition!

The HCSO Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) Team was established in 2016 with a mission to enhance public safety through the strategic use of unmanned aerial technology.
 Since then, the program and its technology have become critical operational assets, providing real-time aerial intelligence, thermal imaging, and rapid response capabilities in support of HCSO patrol, investigations, special operations, emergency management, and regional partner agencies.
 The team has expanded its capabilities to include search and rescue, tactical overwatch, fugitive apprehension, crime scene mapping, disaster assessment, and large-scale event security.
